summary: Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist. He served as Professor of Samskrta at Gujarat Vidyapith and held professorships in Sanskrit at L. D. Arts College and S. L. U. Arts and H. & P. Thakore Commerce College for Women (both attested 1938).

Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar (1909–2001) was an Indologist. He earned an M.A. at the University of Mumbai (~1929–1931) and a doctorate at Heidelberg University (~1936–1938). He held professorships at Fergusson College and Savitribai Phule Pune University, and served as Hon. Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1939–2001).

Ramesh Chandra Negi (born 1956) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He served as a Research Assistant (attested 2001–2004) and Associate Professor (attested 2026) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, teaching Ruth Gamble and Andy Rotman.

Ramesh Chandra Majumdar (1888–1980) was a historian and Indologist educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He held major posts at the University of Dhaka (1921–1942), Banaras Hindu University, and served as president of The Asiatic Society (1966–1968).

Ramesh Shankar Gupte was a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1967, he headed the Department of History & Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and lectured at Wake Forest University, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State University.

Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Lozang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina (attested 2015).
Ramkrishna Bhattacharya (1947–2022) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1966–1969) and served on the faculty at Ananda Mohan College (~1970–2007).
Ramon Prats is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).

Ran Mao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied at Hainan University and earned a PhD from Kasetsart University (2020). He taught Chinese at several international institutions before teaching at Guizhou University of Finance and Economics (2020–2022).
Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under the supervision of Richard Payne and was also taught by Steven D. Goodman.

Randy J. LaPolla (born 1955) is a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (1983–1990) under James Alan Matisoff. He served as a Professor at City University of Hong Kong (~1996–2004) and Beijing Normal University (2021–2023).

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha, and studied under Attaragama Gnanawimala. He is an Associate Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and the 13th Dalai Lama, among others, and taught prominent students including Chögyam Trungpa, Pema Chödrön, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was an Italian scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Ranjeet Kumar Verma works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Lucknow and held a post as a Scholar at the Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad in 2025.
Rano Hodžiakbarovna Guljamova (1940–1985) was an Indologist and linguist. She studied at the National University of Uzbekistan from ~1957 to 1962 and taught there from 1962 until 1985.
Ranu Kunwar pursued PhD studies at the Australian National University (2022–2026) under the supervision of Assa Doron.

Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at Santa Clara University (attested 2012) and served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017).

Raoul Curiel (1913–2000) was a scholar in archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, studying under Sylvain Lévi and Alfred Foucher. He served as Director-General of Pakistan's Department of Archaeology and Museums and as oriental coin curator at the Cabinet des Médailles.
Raphael Kühner (1802–1878) was a linguist who studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (~1821–1824). He was a teacher of Georg Bühler.
